subject.title: [Bug]: macOS app 'Launch at login' stops sticking / appears to turn itself off after app updates

question: Should the macOS app persist OpenClaw-owned Launch at login intent and reconcile app-owned LaunchAgent drift after updates, or should live launchd/System Settings state remain authoritative?
rationale: Current code treats live launchd/plist state as authoritative, while the report asks enabled user intent to survive app replacement/update; changing that can affect user control after external disables.

options.title: Persist intent and reconcile drift
options.body: Store explicit in-app enabled intent and re-register only the app-owned LaunchAgent after startup or update drift, with guards for deliberate OS-level disables.

options.title: Keep launchd authoritative
options.body: Leave live launchd/System Settings state as the source of truth and document that OpenClaw will not restore externally disabled login items.

options.title: Wait for packaged update proof
options.body: Defer implementation until a current-main Sparkle update repro identifies exactly which launchd or UI state flips.

recommendation.title: Persist intent and reconcile drift
recommendation.body: Store explicit in-app enabled intent and re-register only the app-owned LaunchAgent after startup or update drift, with guards for deliberate OS-level disables.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points most strongly to steipete for the original Launch at Login behavior and the earlier persistence fix merge.
